description.narrative: ALCANCE (Programa de Alimentos, Clima, Agricultura, Natureza, Coordenacão e Empoderamento da Mulher) Projektets övergripande mål är att “bidra till att partnerorganisationer får ökad tillgång till produktiv mark, tillgång till och kontroll över produktionsmedel samt ökad kunskap hos kvinnor och småbruksbönder för att säkerställa rätten till näringsrik mat”. Utöver detta har projektet sex övergripande resultatområden: i) Effektivt skäligt och rättvist livsmedelsystem, ii) hållbar försörjning, iii) klimatförändringar och motstånd, iv) jämställdhet, v) skälig och rättvis tillgång till lämpliga bostäder och vi) starkare organisation. ALCANCE projektet kommer, för att uppnå det övergripande målet och resultatet, fokusera på aktiviteter i tre provinser i norra Mocambique: Nampula, Niassa och Cabo Delgado. Huvudsätet för den övergripande programsamordningen för projektet kommer att vara We Effects kontor i Lichinga, Niassa. Genom att rikta in sig på de tre nordligaste provinserna i Mocambique, är det Sidas bedömning att projektet ligger väl i linje med det ökade geografiska fokus som Sveriges strategi för utvecklingssamarbete har valt att fokusera på. Sedan 1991 har We Effect implementerat flertalet program i samband med det svenska utvecklingssamarbetet i Mocambique, med ett första fältkontor i den norra provinsen Niassa som genomförde insatser så som Programa de Apoio a Sociedade Civil -PASC (contribution ID 23000249) och Agricultura e Recursos Naturais - ARENA (contribution ID 51140056). Det största bilaterala samarbetet med den svenska ambassaden var genom Actions for an Inclusive and Accountable Governance (AGIR II), ett projekt som pågick mellan 2010–2020 och som hade följande delprogram: Natural Resources, Agriculture, Climate Change, and Environment (NACE). Vid implementering av NACE, förvaltade We Effect cirka 176 miljoner svenska kronor. År 2020, när AGIR II-programmet slutfördes, kom de överens om en förlängning av NACE-delprogram, till december 2021. ALANCE projektet föreslås implementeras i två etapper. Budgeten för den första fasen som är på två år uppgår till totalt 75,8 MSEK / 456,44 MMZN (1 SEK = 6,017 MZN) och presenteras på kostnadsbasis med sex huvudsakliga rubriker: 66,7 % för fondöverföringar till partners vilket motsvarar 50,6 MSEK (312,2 MMZN) och 33,3 % motsvarande 25,2 MMSEK (144,2 MMZN) för We Effect ledda aktiviteter, övervakning och utvärdering, programpersonalskostnader, programstödskostnader samt administrationskostnader. Ambassaden bedömer att budgeten är rimlig i förhållande till målen och att den förser underlag för ett kostnadseffektivt genomförande av projektet. Då samarbetspartnern kommer inkludera vidarebefordran av medel till tredje part (forwarding of funds) genom olika finansieringsformer, även om We Effect har system för planering, uppföljning, rapportering, utvärdering och lärande på plats, är det ambassadens analys att både den återkommande ekonomiska uppföljningen och den operativa uppföljningen av samarbetspartnerna behöver stärkas för att säkerställa att Sida-medel används på rätt sätt för att uppnå förväntade projektresultat. Sammanfattningsvis bedömer Sida att effekten av ALCANCE bidraget lägger grunden för ett effektivt och rättvist system, hållbar försörjning, förbättrad jämställdhet och motståndskraftiga samhällen i förhållande till klimatförändringarna. Detta genom att partnerorganisationerna ges möjlighet att öka sin tillgång till produktiv mark, tillgång och bättre kontroll över produktionsmedlem samt öka kunskapen hos kvinnor och småbruksbönder om rätten till mat i de tre provinserna som projektet riktar sig till, Niassa, Nampula och Cabo Delgado.

The overall aim of the ALCANCE (Programa de Alimentos, Clima, Agricultura, Natureza, Coordenacão e Empoderamento da Mulher) Contribution is "Empowered partner organisations for increased access to productive land, access, and control of means of production, and increased knowledge by women and stallholder farmers to ensure the right of nutritious food" and, has six overarching results areas (RA) namely: i) Effective equitable and just food systems, ii) Sustainable livelihoods, iii) Climate change and resilience, iv) Gender equality, v) Equitable and just access to adequate housing and vi) Stronger organization. To achieve the overall goal and results, the ALCANCE programme will focus its activities in three provinces located in the northern part of Mozambique namely: Nampula, Niassa and Cabo Delgado. We Effect will use its Lichinga Office in Niassa, as the main hub for the overall programme coordination. Sida assesses that the target provinces are well aligned with the increased geographic focus of the Swedish operationalisation plan. We Effect has been implementing several programmes related to Swedish Development cooperation in Mozambique since 1991, with its first field office in the northern province of Niassa on which implemented interventions such as the Programa de Apoio a Sociedade Civil -PASC (contribution ID 23000249) and the Agricultura e Recursos Naturais - ARENA (contribution ID 51140056). The major bilateral partnership with the Swedish Embassy was through the Actions for an Inclusive and Accountable Governance (AGIR II) programme, 2010-2020 with its sub-programme entitled Natural Resources, Agriculture, Climate Change, and Environment (NACE). For the implementation of NACE, We Effect managed approximately 176 million Swedish Krona. In 2020 as AGIR II programme was being finalized, however an extension of the NACE sub-programme until December 2021 was agreed. The ALCANCE programme is proposed to be implemented in two phases. The budget for the first phase of two years amounts to a total amount of 75, 8 MSEK / 456, 44 MMZN (1 SEK = 6,017 MZN), is presented on a cost-basis with 6 main headers: 66,7% for Funds transfers to partners equal to 50,6 MSEK (312,2 MMZN) and 33,3% equal to 25,2 MMSEK (144,2 MMZN) for We Effect lead activities, Monitoring and evaluation, Programme staff costs, Programme support costs and Administration overhead. The Embassy assesses that the budget is reasonable in relation to the objectives and provides for a basis for a cost-efficient implementation of the programme. Since the cooperation partner will have a component of forwarding of funds to third parties’ trough different funding modalities, even though We Effect has systems for planning, monitoring, reporting, evaluation and learning in place, the Embassy's analysis is that both the recurring financial monitoring and operational monitoring of the partners need to be strengthened to ensure that Sida funding is applied properly to achieve the expected programme results. In conclusion, Sida assesses that the impact of the ALCANCE contribution, lay the ground for an effective, equitable and systems, sustainable livelihoods, improved gender equality and resilient communities to climate change through empowering partner organizations to increase their access to productive land, access and better control of the means of productions as well as increasing the knowledge by women and smallholders farmers about the right to food of three target provinces, Niassa, Nampula and Cabo Delgado.

The overall aim of the ALCANCE program is "Empowered partner organisations for increased access to productive land, access, and control of means of production, and increased knowledge by women and smallholder farmers to ensure the right of nutritious food".
The programme has six overarching results areas:
RA1: Effective equitable and just food systems
RA2: Sustainable livelihoods.
RA3: Climate change and resilience
RA4: Gender equality
RA5: Equitable and just access to adequate housing
RA6: Stronger organisations
Alcance focus its activities in the three northern provinces (Nampula, Niassa and Cabo Delgado), and is implemented jointly with 10 implementing organizations/partners. The theory of change is based on the value of strengthening these local organisations to be effective and sustainable both as organisations and in their relevant role to deliver results as the key drivers and influencers of the change toward a rights-based society. We Effect and partners are working towards the above mentioned six results areas, to achieve fundamental structural changes at individual, household, community, organisational, policy and state levels, to empower smallholder farmer, especially women, youth and other marginalized groups to access/have the right to just and adequate, sustainable and nutritious food.

description.narrative:
Examples of specific results per result area
1) Effective, equitable and just food systems
- 4 020 small holder farmers (2 544 women and 1 476 men), were trained in SALM (sustainable land management) packages, mostly agroecology, conservation agriculture, plant nutrition, production of organic fertilizers for soil improvement, sustainable soil management, post-harvest management.
- 1 680 smallholder farmers (1 026 women and 654 men) benefitted from various agricultural inputs (seeds, tools and pesticides) to boost the increase in production and productivity.
- 16 smallholder farmers were trained in managing manual and mechanized irrigation systems. After the training, these farmers used seven hectares of land and produced maize and various vegetables to improve their familys food security.
- 32 Community Agribusiness Agents (ACAs) and 300 Lead Producers (of whom 150 are women) were trained, and are expected to assist with the connection between smallholders and buyers.
- three Solar power irrigation systems were acquired, to be used by farmers, covering 15 hectares of land.
2) Sustainable livelihoods
- 20 small farmer associations (members of UDACC) have been linked to the cotton company Joao Fereira dos Santos and received agricultural services from private sector providers (inputs on Soya and discussion of market).
- six new cooperatives have been created (all 299 members are women). These and other cooperatives received trainings in family financial management, savings; loans, investment; agricultural insurance; financial management in groups, associations or cooperatives function.
- 30 women received trainings in Processing, Conservation, and Storage of Agricultural Products, aiming at enhancing value chain skills, reducing post-harvest losses, and ensuring sustainable livelihoods for women, families, and communities.
- Three fishermen committees were established by AENA, with a strong focus on including and promoting women's participation in the fish value chain.
- 2 130 women were actively participating in established VSLAs, managing to save an estimated MZN 4,625,792.00 (82% of savers being women). So far, ten women have started small businesses through these savings groups.
3) Climate change and resilience
- Lobbying and advocacy meetings with policymakers to improve policies and practices on climate change adaptation and mitigation, as well as participation in the elaboration of the district Economic and Social Plan and State Budget (PESOD) regarding the integration of environmental protection and climate change actions (Mossuril district).
- memorandums of understanding have been signed with the National Institute for Management and Reduction of Disaster Risks INGD in Cuamba, and with the community radio, as effective ways of transmitting information in mass to the community.
- 140 young people (59% female) were trained in environment, climate change and resilience, to be future environmental educators and community mobilisers.
- 30 journalists were trained from the three community radios on aspects of the environment and climate change, Advance Notice and Reporting Mechanisms.
- 564 women were trained in resilient agriculture techniques by UDACC and AENA, including training of trainers.
- five agroforestry centers were established in Nampula province, to benefit about 138 beneficiaries (85 women) to adopt sustainable agricultural practices in their fields, making the combination of food and forest crops in the same field.
- In Nampula province, AENA contributed to an increase of three hectares of mangroves.
4) Gender equality
- An MOU has been signed with the provincial command of the PRM of Niassa to monitor cases of GBV and disseminate laws that defend women's right and also ensure that the policy offices at the district level collaborate with the FOFeN in awareness-raising, reporting and monitoring of cases GBV.
- AMIREMO promoted two focus group discussion on social norms that increases womens vulnerability at community level, leading to a decision to establish at community level an association to discuss issues related to early marriage. The association will be called "Chinamwali Association
- ACABE promoted nine community dialogue sections on gender equality involving about 352 people from which 150 women, 67 female youths, 103 men and 32 female youth.
- Partners, also did a lot of awareness campaigns related to GBV on the 16 days of activism.
5) Equitable and just access to adequate housing
- FOFeN launched a tender for hiring a consultant to assist on the consultation process for the design of the house models including risk assessment on them. Partners also initiated communications with the Ministry of Public Works, Habitat and water resources (MOPHRH) and UN-HABITAT, for future joint activities.
- FoFeN initiated a participatory consultation process in the communities and villages of Metarica, Maua and Nipepe districts, aiming to develop a typical model of housing resistant to climate change taking into account affordability, habitability and resilience. Drafts of two housing models have been designed and are currently being evaluated.
6) Stronger organisations
- Eight of ten Partners conducted their AGMs. All ten partners received trainings on finance and administration, and have been supported to strengthen their monitoring systems and revised their LFAs.
